chunks: She said: 'Surely when kings enter a city they destroy it and despoil the honour of its nobility. So will they do (to us).'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a city and its nobility when kings enter it according to this narration?
ai.summary: This narration, often cited in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the nature of unjust rule, highlights the systemic corruption and social inversion characteristic of tyrannical leadership. It serves as a theological critique of political power, illustrating how authority, when divorced from justice, leads to the degradation of societal elites and the widespread moral decay of the conquered populace.
